page: Amazon Web Services g5.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 16 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, 250 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Primary acceleration is delivered via a dedicated NVIDIA Ampere A10G GPU equipped with 22 GB of video memory.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate clear bifurcation between host CPU limitations and accelerated compute efficiency. In standard general-purpose metrics, the 4 vCPUs demonstrate modest performance: Geekbench single-core scored 1333.0 (middle 50%) and multi-core scored 3052.0 (bottom 25%), while stress-ng recorded bottom 10% rankings in both single-core (767.0) and multi-core (1532.66) operations. PassMark CPU scored 5636.52, and Redis set operations reached 3.79 million ops/second, aligning with the bottom 25% percentile.

Conversely, the bundled NVIDIA A10G GPU achieves top-tier results in machine learning inference benchmarks. In prompt processing for a 135M parameter model, throughput reached 9337.99 tokens/second alongside 409.6 tokens/second in generation. With a medium 7B model, the GPU delivered 2889.75 tokens/second for prompt ingestion and 94.25 tokens/second during text generation, placing both results in the top 10% tier.

From an architectural tradeoff perspective, the g5.xlarge provides cost-effective access to modern GPU resources without the overhead of massive multi-GPU nodes. The limited core count and baseline network cap of 2 Gbps make it unsuited for CPU-bound data pipelines or distributed cluster coordination. Rather, it is purpose-built for low-latency deep learning inference, small-to-midsize LLM deployment, ray tracing, and remote graphics workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services g5.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance designed for machine learning inference and graphics-intensive tasks. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 4 vCPUs derived from an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor at 3.3 GHz, 16 GB of DDR4 memory, and 250 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Hardware acceleration is provided by a dedicated NVIDIA A10G GPU with 22 GB of VRAM. Benchmark results exhibit distinct operational tiers: while raw CPU and memory metrics rank in the lower percentiles across stress-ng and Geekbench tests, LLM inference throughput achieves top-tier performance, processing 2889.75 tokens per second on prompt ingestion with a 7B parameter model. With 2 Gbps baseline networking, the g5.xlarge provides a resource profile balanced specifically for deep learning inference, image processing, ray tracing, and localized graphics rendering rather than CPU-heavy computing workloads.
